r01.

**Premise correction:** There is no Redis anywhere in this repository. It's a Go project (`github.com/usememos/memos`), and a search of the source, `go.mod`, and `go.sum` turns up zero references to Redis, `ioredis`, `REDIS_URL`, or any external cache server. The cache layer is a hand-rolled, thread-safe **in-process in-memory cache**, so there is no connection to configure.

**Actual mechanism:**

- The cache implementation lives in `store/cache/cache.go` — a `Cache` struct backed by a `sync.Map` with per-item expiration timestamps and a background cleanup goroutine (`store/cache/cache.go:66-85`, `cleanupLoop` at `:199-215`). It implements a `Set`/`SetWithTTL`/`Get`/`Delete` interface (`store/cache/cache.go:11-32`); no network client is involved.

- The cache is instantiated inside the store constructor, not from any Redis config. `Store.New` builds a `cache.Config` and creates three separate in-memory caches — including the user cache — in `store/store.go:40-53`:
  ```go
  cacheConfig := cache.Config{
      DefaultTTL:      10 * time.Minute,
      CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute,
      MaxItems:        1000,
      OnEviction:      nil,
  }
  ...
  userCache: cache.New(cacheConfig),
  ```

- **TTL for user entries:** User records are written with `s.userCache.Set(...)` (`store/user.go:98, 122, 132, 143, 167`). `Set` applies the cache's `DefaultTTL` (`store/cache/cache.go:92-95`), which for the user cache is the **10 minutes** configured in `store/store.go:41`. No user-specific `SetWithTTL` override exists, so user cache entries expire 10 minutes after they're written (with lazy expiry on `Get` at `store/cache/cache.go:135-144` and a sweep every 5 minutes via `CleanupInterval`). Entries are also invalidated explicitly on user deletion (`store/user_delete.go:40`).

(The same package has an unrelated helper `store/cache.go` that only builds user-setting cache-key strings — not a Redis connection either.)

**Redis is NOT used anywhere in this repository.** A full search for `redis`, `ioredis`, `REDIS_URL`, `memcache`, and connection strings across all files (Go, TS/JS, JSON, YAML, env, docs) returned zero matches. There is no Redis connection to configure. This is the `memos` project — a Go backend with a React/TS frontend, and the cache layer is a **custom thread-safe in-memory cache** (a `sync.Map` with per-item TTL and a background cleanup goroutine).

### What caching is actually used

**1. Cache implementation — `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go`**

A hand-rolled in-memory cache (no external library, not even an LRU package). Key structure:
- `Config` struct (lines 42-54): `DefaultTTL`, `CleanupInterval`, `MaxItems`, `OnEviction`.
- `DefaultConfig()` (lines 57-64): `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`, `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute`, `MaxItems: 1000`.
- `Cache` backed by `sync.Map` with an `atomic.Int64` item count (lines 66-73).
- `Set` uses the default TTL; `SetWithTTL` allows a custom TTL (lines 92-120). Expiration is stored as an absolute `time.Now().Add(ttl)` on each `item` (lines 34-39, 110-114).
- Expiry is enforced lazily on `Get` (lines 135-144) and proactively via `cleanupLoop`/`cleanup` on the `CleanupInterval` ticker (lines 199-250). `cleanupOldest` evicts ~20% when over `MaxItems` (lines 253-313).

**2. Where the cache (and thus the "connection") is configured — `/bench/repo/store/store.go`**

There is no network connection; the caches are instantiated in `store.New()` (lines 38-61):

```go
// Default cache settings
cacheConfig := cache.Config{
    DefaultTTL:      10 * time.Minute,
    CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute,
    MaxItems:        1000,
    OnEviction:      nil,
}

store := &Store{
    ...
    instanceSettingCache: cache.New(cacheConfig),
    userCache:            cache.New(cacheConfig),
    userSettingCache:     cache.New(cacheConfig),
    ...
}
```

Three separate cache instances (lines 27-29): `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache`. All are closed in `Store.Close()` (lines 72-79).

### TTL for user entries

**User entries are cached in `userCache` with the default TTL of 10 minutes.**

In `/bench/repo/store/user.go`, every write of a user to the cache uses `s.userCache.Set(...)` (lines 98, 122, 132, 143, 167) — **not** `SetWithTTL` — so it inherits `DefaultTTL`:

```go
// store/user.go:148-168 — GetUser
if find.ID != nil {
    if cache, ok := s.userCache.Get(ctx, userCacheKey(*find.ID)); ok {
        user, ok := cache.(*User)
        if ok {
            return user, nil
        }
    }
}
...
s.userCache.Set(ctx, userCacheKey(user.ID), user)   // uses DefaultTTL
```

`Set` → `SetWithTTL(ctx, key, value, c.config.DefaultTTL)` (cache.go line 93-95), and `DefaultTTL` is `10 * time.Minute` (store.go line 41). Cache key is just the user ID as a string (`userCacheKey`, user.go lines 88-90). User cache invalidation on delete happens via `s.deleteUserCache(...)` (user.go line 179).

**So: user cache entries live for 10 minutes**, are capped at 1000 items (LRU-ish eviction of the oldest ~20% when exceeded), and are swept every 5 minutes by the cleanup goroutine.
